_comment: THE SHOOTOUT GRAPH. tts_audio_suite splits every engine into a config node returning a TTS_ENGINE, which plugs into one UnifiedTTSTextNode. So swapping models means replacing node 1 and touching nothing else - the text, the chunking, the seed and the encoder all stay identical. That is the whole reason this rig exists: a benchmark where each lane has its own bespoke graph measures the graphs, not the models.
_how_to_swap: Change node 1's class_type to another engine and adjust its inputs. Verified class names: Qwen3TTSEngineNode, VibeVoiceEngineNode, ChatterBoxEngineNode, ChatterBoxOfficial23LangEngineNode, CosyVoiceEngineNode, IndexTTSEngineNode, HiggsAudioEngineNode, HiggsAudioV3EngineNode, F5TTSEngineNode, EchoTTSEngineNode, DotsTTSEngineNode, MossTTSEngineNode, StepAudioEditXEngineNode, FishAudioS2EngineNode, OmniVoiceEngineNode, DramaBoxEngineNode, RVCEngineNode.
_licence_gate: DO NOT ship client audio from F5TTSEngineNode (weights cc-by-nc-4.0), HiggsAudioV3EngineNode (research/non-commercial), FishAudioS2EngineNode (research-only) or IndexTTSEngineNode (bespoke bilibili licence). They are in the dropdown because knowing what we give up is the point of benchmarking - not because they are usable. The licence column in stack-docs/VOICE-BENCHMARK.md is the control.
_running_it: Do not hand-edit the text. `bash bench.sh <endpoint-id> workflows/shootout.json <label>` splices the canonical script in and records timing to bench-results.tsv. `BENCH_LANG=FR bash bench.sh ...` runs the French pass.
_schema_drift: Input names below were read from the suite at v5.8.10 and WILL drift - it ships new engines monthly. If the graph 400s on validation, GET /object_info from a running instance and re-read the schema rather than guessing. Every engine node returns TTS_ENGINE, so the wiring in node 2 is the stable part.
